epithet: More, and more — until the graves
lede: The race to have more than the next person is so absorbing that most people only stop running it when they are buried. This surah says so in two ayat, and spends the other six on what they will find out.

names.name: al-Takāthur
names.note: Competing to have more, and boasting of it: wealth, children, followers, numbers of any kind. The Prophet ﷺ was heard reciting it by its opening words, Alhākumu l-takāthur (Muslim 2958).

revelation.detail: Al-Qurṭubī says it is Makkan in the saying of all the commentators, and adds that al-Bukhārī narrated what indicates it is Madinan — a report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb about a saying they had taken for Qurʾan until “Alhākumu l-takāthur” came down. Ibn al-Jawzī gives two accounts of its occasion and they point in the same two directions: one about clans of Quraysh, the other about Jews in Madinah.
revelation.when: The early years in Makkah, among a people who counted their worth by their numbers

evidence.quote: وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ جَمِيعِ الْمُفَسِّرِينَ. وَرَوَى الْبُخَارِيُّ أَنَّهَا مَدَنِيَّةٌ. وَهِيَ ثمان آيات

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ بِمَكَّةَ سُورَةُ ﴿ألْهاكُمُ التَّكاثُرُ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn Mardawayh.

setting: Quraysh were merchants, and their society ran on standing: whose clan was larger, whose caravans richer, whose dead more famous. Ibn al-Jawzī relates that two clans — Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm — fell to arguing over which of them had more chiefs and more men, counted their living, and when that did not settle it went out to the graveyard to count their dead.{reported}

Whether or not that was the very occasion, it is the habit the surah names. Alhākum: it has distracted you — taken you away from what mattered. And it will go on doing so until you visit the graves. The Arabic word is visit, and the early Muslims heard what it implies: a visitor does not stay.

Then the tone changes. No — you will come to know. Again, no — you will come to know. If you knew now, with certain knowledge, you would not be as you are. You will see the Fire with your own eyes. And then you will be asked about every comfort you were given.

occasions.title: Counting the dead
occasions.text: Two reports are given. In one, from Qatādah, some of the Jews said, “We are more than the sons of so-and-so,” and were kept busy with that until they died astray. In the other, two clans of Quraysh, Banū ʿAbd Manāf and Banū Sahm, quarrelled over which had more chiefs and greater numbers, until they went to count those in their graves.
occasions.source: Ibn al-Jawzī, at the head of the surah.

evidence.quote: وَفِي سَبَبِ نُزُولِها قَوْلانِ. أحَدُهُما: أنَّ اليَهُودَ قالُوا: نَحْنُ أكْثَرُ مِن بَنِي فُلانٍ، وبَنُو فُلانٍ أكْثَرُ مَن بَنِي فُلانٍ، فَألْهاهم ذَلِكَ حَتّى ماتُوا ضُلّالًا، فَنَزَلَتْ هَذِهِ فِيهِمْ، قالَهُ قَتادَةُ

aim: To remind those taken up with this world of death, and of the Reckoning.

outline.title: The diagnosis
outline.summary: Rivalry in piling up has distracted you, until you visit the graves.

outline.title: The warning
outline.summary: No — you will come to know. Then no — you will come to know. No — if only you knew with the knowledge of certainty.

outline.title: What is coming
outline.summary: You will surely see Hellfire; then you will see it with the eye of certainty. Then, on that Day, you will be asked about the delights you enjoyed (102:8).

keyAyah.why: The last word of the surah, and the one the Prophet ﷺ brought home over a meal of dates and cold water.

virtues.text: ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Shikhkhīr said: I came to the Prophet ﷺ while he was reciting “Alhākumu l-takāthur”, and he said: “The son of Ādam says: my wealth, my wealth. And do you have anything of your wealth, son of Ādam, except what you ate and used up, or wore and wore out, or gave in charity and sent on ahead?”

The Prophet ﷺ, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar went out one day driven by hunger, and a man of the Anṣār brought them dates, slaughtered a sheep for them, and gave them water. When they had eaten and drunk their fill he ﷺ said: “By the One in whose hand is my soul, you will be asked about this delight on the Day of Resurrection.”

before: Al-Qāriʿah ended with the scales, heavy or light. Al-Takāthur says what makes them light: a life spent adding to the wrong side.
after: Al-ʿAṣr gives the answer in three ayat: everyone is at a loss, except those who believe, do right, and hold one another to truth and patience.

notable.label: Distracted, until you visit the graves
You will be asked about the delights
